events.title: Law 4605/2019 adds EUR 400,000 financial-investment routes
events.description: TI Greece: from November 2019 residence permits could be obtained with EUR 400,000 in financial instruments and companies (deposits, REICs, government bonds, funds) or EUR 800,000 in shares or corporate bonds.

events.title: First golden visa for a long-term bank deposit issued

events.quote: Η πρώτη Golden Visa για μακροπρόθεσμη κατάθεση εκδόθηκε τον Ιούνιο του 2020.

events.title: POS card payments from China for golden-visa flats come to light
events.description: In October 2018 it emerged that Chinese authorities had asked for help investigating breaches of capital controls: a Greek company had placed POS terminals of three Greek banks in China to take card payments for Greek flats bought for golden visas. A bank executive resigned and prosecutors investigated.
events.quote: Η υπόθεση ήρθε στο φως τον Οκτώβριο του 2018

events.title: Law 4589/2019: full price payable at signing, by crossed cheque or bank transfer
events.description: An amendment tabled in January 2019 required the price of property (or tourist-lease) of at least EUR 250,000 to be paid in full at contract signing by crossed cheque or transfer, presented as an anti-money-laundering measure.
events.quote: τροπολογία των Yπουργείων Οικονομίας, Επικρατείας και Μετανάστευσης και Ασύλου, που κατατέθηκε τον Ιανουάριο του 2019 (ν. 4589/2019)

events.title: Law 4635/2019 allows POS card payments, retroactive to 1 January 2017
events.description: TI Greece: the "Invest in Greece" law added payment by card through a POS of a provider operating in Greece, with retroactive effect from 1 Jan 2017, legalising the earlier POS transactions after the fact. The report says it was passed "a few months" after the January 2019 amendment; no exact date given.
events.quote: Η ρύθμιση μάλιστα έχει αναδρομική ισχύ ξεκινώντας από την 1/1/2017.

events.title: POS case archived without charges
events.description: On 2 November 2020 it became known that the justice system had archived the POS case, finding no evidence for prosecution for tax evasion or money laundering.
events.quote: Στις 2 Νοεμβρίου 2020, ήτοι δύο χρόνια αφότου ήρθε στη δημοσιότητα η υπόθεση με τα POS, έγινε γνωστό ότι η Δικαιοσύνη έθεσε στο αρχείο την υπόθεση

events.title: Law 4764/2020 allows remote golden visa applications during COVID-19
events.description: Applicants who had completed their investment could apply remotely, give biometrics later and collect permits through their lawyers with a certified passport copy.
events.quote: Δίνει την επιλογή στους αιτούντες Golden Visa να υποβάλουν την αίτησή τους εξ αποστάσεως, εφόσον έχουν ήδη ολοκληρώσει την επένδυσή τους.

ledger.contains: UAE Cabinet statement as reported by Al Khaleej (2 Jan 2025): 500,000 golden residences issued in the past year; also 23 million visas/entry permits, 150 million visitors, hotel guests and nights (general immigration and tourism, out of scope).

PM Browne on about 150 citizenships and about $50m since the June 2014 election, a goal of about US$10m a month, and a US$200,000 NDF add-on for buyers of a UAE villa project. CIU repost dated 10 Aug 2015; content looks like late 2014.

Carinthia asked in 2009 for three Russian hotel investors (EUR 6m Tibet project) to be naturalised; the Council of Ministers rejected it about a week after 7 Jul 2009. Party-politics figures (BZÖ signatures, members) out of scope. Investors' names not recorded.

Around 2,000 / more than 1,800 Golden Residency beneficiaries Feb-Jun 2022; launch on 7 Feb 2022; categories, BD200,000 property threshold, salary and pension thresholds, 90-day presence, BD300 fee and BD4 application fee.

Minister on the Immigration (Amendment) Bill 2021: current $750,000 home route; proposed "at least $1m" non-real-estate floor, 90-day presence, 10-year holding, deemed approval after three months. Illustrative amounts ($350,000 condo, $5m-$10m capital) and reader comments not recorded.
Kuwaiti official says Bidun could be offered Comoros economic citizenship. Bidun population figures (100,000; 34,000) are about Kuwait, out of scope.

Reuters investigation: 155 passports cancelled Jan 2018 (more than 100 Iranian holders), more than 1,000 Iran-born buyers 2008-2017, more than 300 sold to Iranians under Sambi, at least $100m missing per the parliamentary report; Bidoon scheme background. "Several hundred million dollars" expected and "hundreds"/"thousands" of passports are not numbers. Named private buyers not recorded.

Trade-press summary of the IMF 2024 Article IV: CBI revenue 37% of GDP FY2022/23 (+more than 7 points), IMI's own estimate of about US$232m. Real GDP growth and current account figures are general macro, out of scope.
Report of five PM decrees published in the Gazette on 4 Aug 2022; decree 2653/2022 grants Egyptian nationality to 15 persons. The other four decrees (land allocations) are out of scope.

TI Greece report (2021): investor permits per year 2014-2020 and cumulative (charts), 8,011 investors and over 23,758 family permits to Jul 2020, nationality shares (pie chart), average growth 90%, legal changes 2014-2020 (Laws 4251/2014, 4332/2015, 4589/2019, 4605/2019, 4635/2019, 4764/2020) with thresholds, POS case 2018-2020. Illustrative overpricing example (EUR 80,000/160,000/250,000) and VICE's ~300 contracts reviewed are anecdotes, not programme figures.

444/Direkt36: 16 settlement permits revoked (5 investors, 11 family) with a table by month and nationality, 19,838 participants, bond price range EUR 250-300,000, no Syrians among revocations. Names of private individuals not recorded.

TI Hungary/KFIB study (2018): series table (issue/maturity dates, yields, year-end outstanding 2013-2017), relative cost per series vs market bonds and vs EIB loans, proceeds by year and total, shares of financing need/debt/FX debt, 8 intermediaries (3 revoked), 6,621 bonds, 19,855 permit holders, bond terms. 16 charts have no printed values. Macro figures (deficit, debt repayment, KESZ, reserves, EIB lending) out of scope; "about 90% issue price" is an illustrative calculation.

GLOBALCIT country report on Cape Verde (Jan 2026): history of the 1992 investor quasi-citizenship (Laws 41/IV/92, 64/IV/92, DL 53/93), the 2023 Nationality Act Art. 14 on citizenship by investment, Art. 60 of the 2024 Regulation on effective ties, pending investment regulation. No statistics. Rest is general nationality law, out of scope.

RTÉ (15 Apr 2025): EUR 500m since closure, 2,472 / 2,482 approved applications, EUR 1.7bn, China 2,332 (94%), US 53, about 30% in last two years, 83 post-closure projects, 100 applications/1,700 investors in process, over 140 new projects after the closure announcement; investment options and net worth; closure 15 Feb 2023.

Straits Times/OCCRP: Cambodia stopped publishing naturalisations (last Feb 2024); about 50 a month Jan 2020-Aug 2023, four Sep-Dec 2023; US$300,000 investment / US$250,000 donation routes. "17 associates" held Cambodian passports (not a programme count); $3bn laundering case out of scope. Names of private individuals not recorded.

IMI Daily summary of the CIU FY2023/24 annual report: applications received/approved/denied, revenue and cost lines, surplus, remittances, balance sheet items, due-diligence provider counts and residence splits, FY25 targets, IMI processing-time tool. IMI's ratio "18 times" (from two extracted figures), "tripled", the 0.05% bank fee and the RICO/UK-visa context are not recorded as numbers.

Monitorul Fiscal (2 Mar 2020): government approves draft law for a repeat moratorium to 1 Jan 2021; earlier extension to 24 Feb 2020; Law 107/2019 of 31 Jul 2019 with an initial four-month moratorium.
Marshall Islands Journal archive column: 22 Jun 1996 item "Passport sales halted" (Cabinet suspension announced 20 Jun 1996). Other items on the page are unrelated.

Minister's statement on Residency Malta 2022: more than EUR 50m overall, MPRP 780 applications and EUR 33.4m with its split, 3,580 applications and EUR 51m since 2016. Nomad Residence Permit and Start-up Residence figures (500 / 668 applications, EUR 84,000 salary, EUR 16.8m impact) are not investment programmes, out of scope.
